2027-02-18.title: Thursday of the First Week of Lent
readings: Esther C:12, 14–16, 23–25 (Greek additions; in many Bibles 14:1, 3–5, 12–14)
I have no helper but you, O Lord
Lord, on the day I called for help, you answered me
2027-02-18.alt: Lenten weekday, First Week of Lent. The Alleluia is omitted throughout Lent; the Gloria is omitted except on solemnities and feasts. Liturgical colour: violet.
2027-02-18.verse: “Ask, and it will be given you; search, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened for you.
theo: Queen Esther stands at the edge of a terrible choice. A royal decree has ordered the destruction of her whole people, the Jews of Persia, and only she can plead with the king. But to enter his presence uninvited is to risk death. Before she goes, she fasts, lays aside her royal robes, covers her head with ashes, and lies on the ground in prayer: “O my Lord, you only are our king; help me, who am alone and have no helper but you, for my danger is in my hand.” She remembers how God chose Israel from among all the nations and kept every promise. Then she asks for courage and the right words: “Remember, O Lord; make yourself known in this time of our affliction, and give me courage… Put eloquent speech in my mouth before the lion.” This is how the saints pray when everything depends on God: humbly, remembering his faithfulness, and asking boldly. Her prayer is answered; the king's heart is turned, and her people are saved.

In the Gospel Jesus encourages exactly this kind of prayer. “Ask, and it will be given you; search, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened for you.” Three verbs, each a little more persistent than the last. Then he appeals to every parent's heart: “Is there anyone among you who, if your child asks for bread, will give a stone?… If you then, who are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask him!” God is not a reluctant official who must be pestered; he is a Father who loves to give. And the passage ends with the Golden Rule: “In everything do to others as you would have them do to you; for this is the law and the prophets.” The one who receives generously from the Father learns to give generously to others. Lenten prayer and Lenten charity are one movement of the heart.
outline: Ask: what do you do when you are alone and in danger?
Esther's prayer in the hour of danger.
Persistent prayer to a loving Father.
The Golden Rule as the fruit of prayer.
“Ask, and it will be given you.”
live: Bring to God today the one request you have been afraid to ask.
Before each conversation today, ask: how would I want to be treated?
2027-02-18.prayer: Lord our King, you heard Queen Esther when she was alone and had no helper but you. Hear us when we call on you in our need. Teach us to ask, to search and to knock with the trust of children, and to give to others the goodness we long to receive from you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: At Mass we ask, and the Father gives us not a stone but the true Bread from heaven: his own Son.

quick: Queen Esther, alone and in danger, prays to God for courage and help.
Jesus says: ask, search, knock; the Father gives good things.
Treat others as you want to be treated.
2027-02-18.action: Bring God the request you have been afraid to ask.
2027-02-18.question: Do I pray as a child who trusts the Father, or as a stranger who doubts?

family.explain: Jesus says: ask God, and he will give you what is good. If Mummy and Daddy give good things to their children, God our Father gives even better things!
family.intention: We pray for people who are afraid and alone.
family.ask: Ask: “What do we want to ask God for together tonight?”

illus: A nurse from Kottayam working in the Gulf found herself trapped by an employer who took her passport and would not pay her. She had no family nearby and no one to call. She said later that she prayed only one line, over and over: Lord, I have no helper but you. A Malayali priest she met at Sunday Mass put her in touch with the embassy. Three months later she was home. She now volunteers with a group that helps migrant workers in the same trouble.

pm.open: Lord, you are our King and our only help. Hear us when we call, and give us courage. Amen.
share: Help me, who am alone and have no helper but you (Esther C:14). When did I last pray like this?
Ask, search, knock (Matthew 7:7). Do I give up too easily in prayer?
Do to others as you would have them do to you (Matthew 7:12). Whom have I treated as I would not want to be treated?
pm.resp: Lord, on the day I called for help, you answered me.
interc: For persecuted minorities and peoples in danger.
For migrant workers who are exploited and alone.
For women in positions of risk and responsibility.
For those who have stopped believing that God hears them.
For our group, that we may pray with persistence and trust.
pm.close: Father, you give good things to those who ask you. Make us bold in prayer and generous in charity. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Queen Esther knew her people were about to be destroyed. Before going to the king, she lay on the ground in prayer: O my Lord, you only are our king; help me, who am alone and have no helper but you (Esther C:14).
She did not pretend to be strong. She remembered God's faithfulness and asked for courage and the right words. And God turned the king's heart. Prayer from the depths is never wasted.

Jesus says: ask, and it will be given you; search, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened for you (Matthew 7:7). If you then, who are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask him! (Matthew 7:11).
And Jesus adds: in everything do to others as you would have them do to you (Matthew 7:12). Let us ask the Father with trust today, and then give to others what we hope to receive. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says: ask God for what you need, and he will give you good things, because he is your Father. Tonight, ask God for something for someone else, and trust him.

intro: Theme: “Ask, and it will be given you.”
Esther's lonely prayer, the persistence Jesus asks of us, and the Golden Rule.

q: On the day I called, you answered me, you increased my strength of soul.
Let us therefore approach the throne of grace with boldness, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help in time of need.
points.apply: Bring your greatest fear to God in prayer today, in your own words.

q: When you search for me, you will find me; if you seek me with all your heart,
“Ask, and it will be given you; search, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened for you.
points.apply: Keep praying for one intention every day until Easter.

q: And what you hate, do not do to anyone.
“In everything do to others as you would have them do to you; for this is the law and the prophets.
points.apply: Do for someone today what you would want done for you.

concl: God is a Father who loves to give.
The one who receives learns to give.
2027-02-18.resolve: Choose one intention to pray for daily this Lent, and one person to serve.
